messages:
Maya Chen: FYI — evals pipeline just flagged a regression on the Traditional Chinese vertical-OCR set after we rolled the new quantized bring-up (redwood/llm-v2-int4).
Jun Park: saw that, can you paste the quick diff / sample? :eyes:
Maya Chen: summary: BLEU down ~7.8 points vs baseline on vertical layout samples from our OCR partner. Mostly on punctuation and line-break detok — model inserts extra spaces around fullwidth punctuation and drops ruby annotations.
Maya Chen: sample (baseline -> new):
```
# source vertical OCR (visual line segments joined):
我
的：
測
試

Baseline detok: "我的：測試"
New model detok: "我 的 ： 測 試"
```
Akira Saito: wow, spaces between CJK chars — sounds like tokenization normalization changed somewhere.
Zheng Li: could be unicode normalization or a pyicu change in tokenizer preprocessor. Any chance the pipeline used NFKC vs NFD recently?
Maya Chen: our onboarding script for v2 toggled `normalizer: NFKC` for compatibility with some western punctuation fixes. I ran a local tokenization dump:
```
# tokenizer.dump for sample "我的：測試"
baseline.tokens -> ["我的", "：", "測試"]
v2-int4.tokens -> ["我", "的", "：", "測", "試"]
```
Liam O'Connor: that split is huge. If the tokenizer changed, BLEU drop makes sense. Was tokenizer regenerated with SentencePiece training on mixed fullwidth+latin data?
Maya Chen: yes, training used mixed layout data to cover vertical OCR cases — but I didn't expect it to split common compounds.
Jun Park: also worth checking quantization path: int4 build used different vocab remapping step to reduce embedding table size. If remapping messed up merges, subword boundaries could change at runtime.
Zheng Li: good call — the embedding remap script (scripts/remap_vocab.py) had an option `--merge-rules` that was left on. That could reassign indices and, combined with normalization, explain both token splits and scoring changes.
Akira Saito: quick repro command for anyone who wants to replicate locally:
```
python -m rwinference.evals.run \
  --model redwood/llm-v2-int4 \
  --task vertical_ocr_zh_hant \
  --repro 1 \
  --dump-tokenization out/tokens.txt
```
Maya Chen: dumped tokens and sample outputs in the report: https://redwood.s3/evals/1723456789/report.html (TL;DR attached below)
Jun Park: can we bisect between v2-int4 build and baseline to see whether it's tokenizer or quantization that caused most of the quality delta?
Maya Chen: I tried a quick ablation — same tokenizer + int8 quant -> matches baseline BLEU within 0.6 pts. Different tokenizer + baseline quant -> huge drop. So primary culprit is tokenizer/normalizer change.
Liam O'Connor: ok that's useful. Two remediation paths:
- revert tokenizer normalizer to match baseline (NFKD -> previous behavior)
- keep normalization but retrain sentencepiece with stronger preserve-merge rules (manual merge whitelist)
Zheng Li: also check evaluation detokenizer: detok script `detok/zh_hant.py` has a heuristics flag `collapse_whitespace=True` — maybe it was toggled in the eval harness by accident when we added vertical-layout splitting.
Akira Saito: I've added a short unit test for detok to catch extra-space insertion. PR incoming.
Maya Chen: one more wrinkle — deploy-bot shows canary rolled v2-int4 to staging GPUs yesterday; evals-bot ran nightly job and posted the regression alert at 06:12 UTC.
deploy-bot: canary roll to staging completed (v2-int4) — 6 nodes. :rocket:
evals-bot: nightly-eval: vertical_ocr_zh_hant: BLEU -7.8 (baseline 31.4 -> v2-int4 23.6) — details: https://redwood.s3/evals/1723456789/report.html
Jun Park: let's do this plan: revert tokenizer normalizer to baseline in canary, run the evals.job on staging (fast subset), and hold full rollout until we confirm. I'll open the rollback PR now.
Maya Chen: created issue #ML-1247 with reproducer and attached token dumps. tagging @Jun @Zheng for follow-up. :white_check_mark:
Liam O'Connor: also add a quick check to the onboarding checklist: "verify tokenization parity on language-specific eval sets" — caught too late here.
Akira Saito: PR for detok unit tests: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/4872 — requesting review from @Zheng and @Maya.
Zheng Li: will review. If we want to keep the normalization change for other fixes, we should add merge exceptions for frequent CJK compounds (我的, 今天, 北京, etc.) during sentencepiece training.
Maya Chen: agreed. I'll pause the rollout and run retrain with merge whitelist and per-channel quant (int4) variant to see cost/quality tradeoffs. Thanks all.
Liam O'Connor: great catch, team. :clap:
Maya Chen: marking this thread for the postmortem doc. I'll summarize root cause and remediation steps after we confirm the retrain results.
